text:
Martin Necas is suddenly carrying a lot more of Colorado. With Nathan MacKinnon out at least a month and Cale Makar about two weeks, both hurt in Ottawa, the Avalanche's offense runs through him for now, and he arrives on a good run: 24 points in 21 games and a four-point night against Detroit on Nov. 7.

The goals need a caution label. He has 10 on 6.19 expected (the quality of his chances), shooting 23% against 18% last season and above the top of our range for him; that finishing rate rarely lasts. His last ten games brought 10 points against 10.7 expected, so the overall production is honest. Last season Evolving-Hockey ranked him 11th among forwards in wins above replacement, but also had him with the strongest teammates in the league (99th percentile), which flatters on-ice numbers. That's the question these next few weeks answer. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says he can drive play himself, carrying the puck in on 62% of his entries and setting up shots at a 95th percentile rate. We'd watch whether the Avs' chances with him on the ice hold up without their two stars.
